newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan rights groups denounce prison conditions.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan rights groups denounce prison conditions.

text.p: Two Moroccan human rights groups on Wednesday denounced what they termed "catastrophic" conditions in two prisons and called for an inquiry and urgent talks between officials and prisoners on hunger strike.
The independent Moroccan Association for Human Rights (AMDH) said: "The authorities must move to open a constructive dialogue with the hunger strikers."
In a statement it spoke of "the miserable conditions of those detained, bad food and hygiene, lack of medicines and difficulties over prison visits" by relatives.

It said a total of 25 prisoners had been on hunger strike since early September in Kenitra jail, 30 km (20 miles) north of Rabat, and at Oukacha jail in Casablanca. "They are still on strike," a spokesman said.

Earlier this month, the prisons administration denied reports that Kenitra inmates were being deprived of their rights to medical treatment and access to hospitals. It said doctors had been appointed to the prison and they decided whether inmates should go to hospital.

The AMDH said 20 jailed Moslem fundamentalists in a letter to the league said despite the official announcement "we still suffer from lack of medicines...and the authorities' behaviour undermines and harms our dignity in violation of human rights conventions signed by the Moroccan government."
The small Moroccan League for the Defence of Human Rights (LMDDH) appealed on Wednesday for an urgent inquiry commission into the prisons.

A spokesman said he was unsure if the hunger strike was still on. "It is not an unlimited strike. One group of prisoners goes on hunger strike for three or four days, then another group takes over," he said.
Kenitra prison is Morocco's main jail for long-term prisoners, generally serving sentences of over 10 years.
